notes: The vision endpoint test now reads the worker counts and names the real problem. The first field run of the test revealed an endpoint with 18 requests queued, zero jobs ever completed, and every worker slot throttled — RunPod simply cannot start a GPU for it, which the previous verdict misread as a protocol problem. The test now checks worker health first: when no worker can start, it says so, with the throttled/queued/completed numbers and the exact console fixes (allow more GPU types and datacenters, Max Workers at least 1, check credits, purge the stuck queue). The not-a-vLLM verdict is reserved for endpoints whose workers are alive and still won't chat.
